what: Moderna develops medicines and vaccines based on messenger RNA. Its Covid vaccine made it briefly very profitable; it now sells Covid and RSV vaccines while spending heavily on a pipeline in flu, cancer and rare disease.
customers: Governments and health systems buying vaccines, and pharmacies in commercial markets.
money: Spikevax, now a commercial seasonal product rather than a government contract
moat: A messenger RNA platform and manufacturing capability that can move from genetic sequence to a candidate vaccine in weeks, which few companies can match.
risks: Revenue fell about 40% in the last financial year as Covid demand collapsed
It lost about $2.8 billion over the last twelve months and is burning cash
Vaccination rates in the US have fallen and policy is less supportive
Its pipeline must deliver an approval that sells before cash runs low
opportunities: It holds about $5.2 billion of cash against only $1.2 billion of debt, which buys time
Costs are being cut sharply to reach break-even with a smaller revenue base
Its individualised cancer vaccine with Merck is in late-stage trials, a potentially large market
watch: Cash burn each quarter against the balance, and late-stage trial readouts in flu and oncology.
